claims.text: Optimized Al content in nanoscale Al0.1CrCoFeNi enhances short-range chemical ordering.
Enhanced short-range chemical ordering forms local atomic clusters.
The local atomic clusters impede atomic diffusion.
Impeded diffusion retards phase separation during high-temperature exposure.
Impeded diffusion retards grain coarsening during high-temperature exposure.
The initial alloy is nanocrystalline and contains a distribution of short-range ordered regions.
Changing Al content while holding processing and thermal history constant provides a controlled comparison of the effect of Al content.
The proposed comparison applies to heat treatment at 1000–1200 K in an inert atmosphere.
Short-range chemical ordering can be quantitatively characterized using pair distribution function analysis and high-resolution TEM.
Samples with optimized Al content will retain a stable, single-phase nanostructure after high-temperature treatment.
Samples with optimized Al content will exhibit less grain growth than samples with lower or uncontrolled Al content.
Samples with optimized Al content will exhibit less phase separation and diffusion-driven degradation than baseline samples.
Lower or non-optimized Al content produces less pronounced short-range ordering.
Less pronounced short-range ordering leads to greater grain growth, phase separation, and structural degradation.
The prediction is bounded to temperatures of 1000–1200 K.
Below an unspecified critical initial grain size, diffusion is governed more strongly by short-range chemical clusters than by grain-boundary effects.
Excess Al may trigger formation of secondary phases.
Failure to observe a statistically significant association between Al content and short-range ordering would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure of samples with enhanced ordering to show reduced grain growth and phase separation relative to the baseline would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The material is repeatedly designated Al0.1CrCoFeNi, which fixes the Al stoichiometric coefficient, while the intervention and experimental design describe systematically varying Al content without defining distinct compositions.
